## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.
import { readFileSync, writeFileSync } from 'node:fs';

const shell = readFileSync('src/shell.html', 'utf8');
const css = readFileSync('src/style.css', 'utf8');
const js = readFileSync('src/app.js', 'utf8');
const three = readFileSync('vendor/three.min.js', 'utf8');

function inject(haystack, needle, value) {
  const at = haystack.indexOf(needle);
  if (at < 0) throw new Error(`Missing placeholder ${needle}`);
  return haystack.slice(0, at) + value + haystack.slice(at + needle.length);
}

let out = shell;
out = inject(out, '/*__CSS__*/', css);
out = inject(out, '/*__THREE__*/', three);
out = inject(out, '/*__GAME__*/', js);
writeFileSync('index.html', out);
console.log(`index.html written: ${(out.length / 1024).toFixed(0)} KB`);

## Objective
- Build/improve a complete mobile HTML5 zombie-pinball game (“WUMMI – Zombie Pinball Protocol”) in 9:16, one-finger playable, with ranking, difficulties, sound, animated main menu, powerups, procedural levels, and a detailed animated dachshund, credited to BANDOS7 / Made in Germany / version 1.1.1, delivered as a single copy-paste `index.html`.

## Requirements
- Mobile HTML5, 9:16 portrait, one-finger controls.
- Ranking and multiple difficulty levels.
- Game sound; genuinely animated main menu.
- Pinball + zombie apocalypse + security teams.
- Diverse powerups, procedurally generated levels, extras.
- Dark atmosphere, high visual quality, very detailed dachshund animation.
- Everything clearly visible; playfield not covered by UI.
- Developer BANDOS7, Made in Germany, version 1.1.1.
- Must provide an HTML5 copy-paste version (self-contained file).

## Decisions
- Reused and enhanced the existing Three.js game from `src/shell.html`, `src/style.css`, `src/app.js`, built inline into `index.html` via `node build.mjs`.
- Enforced strict 9:16 app frame with `aspect-ratio: 9 / 16` and min-based sizing.
- Added invisible left/right playfield tap/hold zones for one-finger flipper control; tapping either zone launches a held ball.
- Added bottom-edge-only press feedback so the playfield isn’t visually covered.
- Kept main-menu dog in a fixed three-quarter pose after a patrol/turn experiment produced unattractive rear views and clipping.
- Improved game lighting, playfield texture, ball glow/halo/marker/point-light, back-corner beacons, and camera framing; moved dog forward and enlarged it.
- Prevented zero-score runs from being added to ranking; only rank #1 counts as a new record.
- Added dog sniff/alert/gait animation support and head-follows-ball behavior.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing full game inspected, run, and visually tested at 390×844, 430×764, 360×640, and desktop.
- Strict 9:16 frame implemented.
- One-finger field controls implemented and verified via mouse pointer: tap launches; hold activates flipper and left button.
